subject: Fraud Watch: Business email compromise and vendor payment scams
text:
Fraud Watch | November 2026

Business email compromise (BEC) remains the costliest fraud type our commercial clients face. In the most common version, a criminal impersonates one of your vendors and asks you to update their bank account.

What a typical fraudulent request looks like:

   "Please be advised that we have changed our bank. Kindly update your records and send all outstanding and future payments to our new account below. Routing: XXXXXXXXX Account: XXXXXXXX. Please treat as urgent."

Red flags:
- Urgency, secrecy, or pressure from an executive
- A sender domain that is one character off from the real one
- A request to change bank details by email alone

What to do:
- Never update payment instructions based on email alone.
- Call the vendor back using a phone number you already have on file, not one in the email.
- Require a second person to approve any change to vendor bank details.

To report suspected fraud, call 1-800-555-0177.

Meridian Commercial Bank | Member FDIC
label: ordinary
note: Bank fraud-awareness newsletter that quotes a sample bank-change request verbatim. Describes the attack; asks nothing.
